title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses
summary: Staleness was evaluated only inside the press handler (cullToRecommended), so the rail rendered an enabled, quantified primary action for states the controller would unconditionally refuse. Lifted the whole evaluation into SessionReviewController.cullRecommendationOffer -> CullRecommendationOffer{status: none|stale|alreadyOptimal|offerable, keepN, gainPct}; cullToRecommended() now switches on that same getter, so press-time and render-time cannot disagree. SubCullRail subscribes to the controller and passes onCullToRecommended only when offer.isOfferable; stale/alreadyOptimal render an explanatory status chip ('Cull analysis out of date' / 'Keep-set already optimal') instead of a pressable promise.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_stale_curve_test.dart - 4 full-wiring widget tests over a real in-memory DB + real SessionReviewController (nothing stubbed): stale population -> chip not button; matching population with +0.0% gain -> chip, and cullToRecommended() genuinely returns alreadyOptimal leaving 4 accepted; live gainful curve -> 'Keep best 2 (+7%)' still renders; rejecting a sub retracts the action with the SAME curve object still in state.
revert_check: Reverted the production wiring at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/widgets/sub_cull_rail.dart:288-289, replacing `_offer.isOfferable ? () => _cullToRecommended(_offer) : null` with the pre-fix predicate `_offer.keepN > 0 ? ... : null`. 3 of the 4 tests failed. Restored -> 4/4 pass.
caveats: The chip text is a status, not a remedy; re-integrating is still the way to refresh the curve, but the rail no longer offers a press that will be refused.

title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- byte-identical settings to Balanced
summary: IntegrationSettings.preset(maximumQuality) restated five constructor defaults (lanczos3 / snrSquared / rejection map / cosmetic / f32) that `balanced` already inherits, so the two objects differed only in `sourcePreset`, a chip-highlight label the native path never reads. Replaced the body with knobs that genuinely change the stack and are genuinely forwarded: ransacThresholdPx 1.0 (vs 2.0), maxRefStars 120 (vs 60), normalization local (vs global). Verified the wire: toBridgeSettings() emits all three (align.ransacThresholdPx, align.maxRefStars, normalization.mode) and bridge/src/api/post_session.rs:1764-1768 assigns them into the native align config (cfg.ransac_threshold_px, cfg.max_stars_for_matching). Also made the panel readout name the knobs the active profile changed, so three profiles can no longer render the same sentence.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/integration_settings_panel_test.dart - 'Maximum Quality actually costs something over Balanced' (asserts the three knobs differ from IntegrationSettings.defaults), 'no two integration profiles produce the same stack' (hashes every preset's toBridgeSettings payload across all five presets and fails on any collision - this is the general guard, not just the reported pair), and 'the readout names the knobs the active profile changes' (widget-level: finds 'RANSAC 1.0 px' / 'Max ref stars 120' / 'Normalization Local grid').
revert_check: Restored the pre-fix preset body at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:754-757 (`ransacThresholdPx: 1.0, maxRefStars: 120, normalization: NormalizationMode.local` -> the old `resampler: lanczos3, weighting: snrSquared, generateRejectionMap: true, cosmeticCorrection: true, outputBitDepth: f32`). 3 tests failed, including the payload-collision guard. Restored -> 9/9 pass.
caveats: The knob VALUES are a judgement call (1.0px / 120 stars / local); what the test pins is that the profile is not a no-op and that no two profiles serialize identically.

title: Running an A/B recipe preview leaves a full 'Preview... 100%' progress bar pinned under the header forever
summary: _bindProgress deliberately leaves a terminal 1.0 fraction on state so the bar lands full, and only integrate() ever cleared it. reIntegratePreview() - what the A/B panel's 'Run both' calls - returned without clearing, orphaning the strip. Rather than adding one more per-action clear (which the next action added would forget), introduced SessionReviewController._withLiveProgress(body): a try/finally that tears the strip down on success, failure and every early-out. Every seam-driven action now routes through it: integrate(), reIntegratePreview(), runColorCalibration(), runNarrowband(), and _runFinishingStep() which is the shared body of runBackgroundExtraction/runDeconvolve/runStarReduction.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/session_review_progress_strip_test.dart - drives the real SessionReviewScreen against a real controller and a seam that emits the same terminal (phase:'preview', fraction:1.0) the native preview integrate does (post_session.rs:838), with the same ordering that orphaned the strip. Asserts a control first (a live 0.5 event DOES render 'Preview...', so the finder is not vacuously passing), then that after reIntegratePreview returns both state().progress is null and 'Preview...' is gone from the tree.
revert_check: Severed the wiring at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1122, replacing `return _withLiveProgress(() async {` with `return (() async {` (and the matching `})();`) so reIntegratePreview runs its identical body unwrapped. The test failed. Restored -> passes.

title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result
summary: `await _addStackFrame(...)` sat unguarded inside the followers loop. Every native rejection path (too few stars, too few matches, residual over the ceiling) returns Err, so one refused follower threw out of the loop into the run-level catch, which deleted the partial stacked_results row and rethrew - frames after it were never attempted, and the framesRejected counter twenty lines below was unreachable. Wrapped the await in a try/catch that counts the frame, tallies its reason (SkotiqError.imageError wrapper stripped to the actionable sentence), logs, emits a stacking-phase progress event and continues. Authority loss still rethrows, since that is a genuine run-level abort. A run in which EVERY follower is refused now throws StackAndShareAllFramesRejectedException naming the count and the dominant reason, rather than persisting a one-frame 'stack'. Also scoped the persisted avgHfr to the image ids the engine actually integrated, so a refused sub cannot drag a number it never contributed to.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/stack_and_share_service_test.dart - 'a rejected follower is counted and skipped; the run continues' asserts the engine still received addFile for frames 2,3,4,5 (i.e. 4 and 5 were attempted after 3 threw), that the run reached StackAndSharePhase.complete, that a stacked_results row was genuinely written and readable back through the DAO, and that the last stacking progress carries framesRejected==1 / framesProcessed==5. 'a run whose followers are ALL rejected fails with the dominant reason' pins the one-frame case. 'avgHfr is the mean HFR of the frames the engine integrated' pins the HFR scoping.
revert_check: Severed the guard at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:416, replacing `if (!_hasAuthority) rethrow;` with an unconditional `rethrow;` so a refused follower escapes the loop exactly as before. Both target tests failed. Restored -> 22/22 pass.
caveats: The residual that CAUSED the rejection in the live repro is a separate defect (see the stacking.rs robust-fit entry); this entry only makes a rejection survivable.

title: Registration reports a 10.34px alignment residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field
summary: LiveStacker::add_frame fit the frame->reference transform with a single least-squares Procrustes over EVERY nearest-neighbour pair. match_stars is a greedy brightest-first search with a 50px radius that CONSUMES the frame star it picks, so a reference star the frame detector missed steals a neighbour, that neighbour's true owner is denied and steals another - a cascade of ~45px mis-pairs that drags the fit far enough to report 10.34px on a rigid 2.2px shift. Added fit_transform_robust(): clip pairs whose post-fit deviation exceeds max(3 x MEDIAN deviation, 1.5px) and refit, up to 5 passes, never below max(min_matched_pairs, 3) pairs (a rigid fit has 4 DoF). add_frame now takes (transform, residual, inlier_count) from it, rejects when too few pairs agree on ONE transform, and gates on the inlier RMS. Deliberately did NOT touch match_radius_px: tightening the radius alone would have relocated the defect (frames whose true offset exceeds the new radius would stop matching at all) rather than removing it. With the residual now meaning something, tightened max_alignment_residual_px 10.0 -> 2.0.
test: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs - two tests. `add_frame_survives_a_matcher_cascade_from_missing_stars` is the END-TO-END one that severs cleanly: it builds an 8x8 star grid at 45px pitch (inside the 50px radius), makes the frame a rigid (+2,+1) shift with the three brightest stars ABSENT so the real consume-and-steal cascade fires, runs the real detector + matcher + add_frame, and asserts Ok, frame_count()==2 and rejected_alignment_failures==0. `mis_paired_stars_do_not_wreck_the_transform_fit` is the unit-level one: 24 correct pairs on a rigid translation plus 4 genuine mis-pairs, asserts the NAIVE fit is >5px wrong (so the test is not vacuous) and the robust fit is <0.5px with exactly the 24 correct pairs surviving and the translation recovered to 0.1px.
test_command: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test -p skotiq_imaging --lib stacking
revert_check: Severed the call site at native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs:495-496, replacing `fit_transform_robust(&matches, self.ref_centroid, self.config.min_matched_pairs)` with the pre-fix naive `compute_affine_transform` + `compute_alignment_residual` over all matches. `add_frame_survives_a_matcher_cascade_from_missing_stars` failed with 'Alignment residual too high: 13.96px' - the reported defect, reproduced in-crate. Restored -> 27/27 stacking tests pass, cargo fmt --check clean.
caveats: (1) Lowering the ceiling to 2.0px is a real behaviour change: a frame whose INLIER RMS genuinely exceeds 2px (heavy field rotation or distortion against a rigid model) is now refused where 10.0 accepted it. That is intended - 2px folded into a stack is a visibly smeared image - and it is only survivable because the Stack & Share fix in this same batch turns a per-frame rejection into a skip instead of a run abort. (2) The verifier's caveat (c) - detect_stars returning 0 stars on audit_L_001.fits where an independent peak finder reads 40 - is NOT addressed here; it is a separate detector-sensitivity question, not the fit. The e2e test above shows the mis-pairing mechanism alone reproduces the reported observable. (3) Not re-driven against the original FITS: no hardware/audit profile in this environment.

title: After session recovery the imaging Session card says 'Captured 0 frames' while the line under it says 'Integration 40m 0s'
summary: The two lines read from different records. 'Captured' came from recentSessionFramesProvider -> sessionImagesProvider, a StateNotifier seeded with [] on every app launch (frames captured in THIS run), while 'Integration' came from the restored sessionState.totalIntegrationSecs. SessionService.recoverSession already restores completedExposures = session.successfulExposures alongside it (session_provider.dart:250), so the count was in state and the card ignored it. CapturePanel now derives capturedCount from sessionState.completedExposures whenever a session row is open (dbSessionId != null), falling back to the in-run list only for captures taken with no session. Confirmed completedExposures is not recovery-only: SessionStateNotifier increments it on every completed exposure (session_provider.dart:285, :305), so the card stays live during a normal run too.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/capture_panel_recovered_session_test.dart - pumps the real CapturePanel with sessionStateProvider seeded to exactly what recoverSession restores (dbSessionId 3, completedExposures 8, totalIntegrationSecs 2400), first ASSERTING recentSessionFramesProvider is empty (so the contradiction is genuinely set up), then that '40m 0s' and '8 frames' both render and '0 frames' does not. Second test pins the singular ('1 frame').
revert_check: Severed the selection at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/capture_panel.dart:88, replacing the `sessionState.dbSessionId != null` predicate with `false` so the card falls back to sessionImages.length exactly as before. Both tests failed. Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: The Share Card's metadata strip is clipped: 'M51  Integration 00:35:00  Frames 7  Fil...'
summary: ShareCardRenderer._drawBottomBar laid the caption out as ONE row at a font derived from the image HEIGHT (fontForHeight) and never measured it against the card WIDTH; the only width logic was `if (x >= bitmap.width - pad) break;` after the glyph run had already started, so drawString clipped the last segment mid-word. Added fitCaption(preferred, segments, cardWidth): steps DOWN a font ladder (arial48/24/14, never above the caller's height-derived choice) and greedy-wraps whole 'LABEL value' segments into at most 3 rows, returning the largest font where every segment fits the available width. Segments are never split - splitting one is what produced the truncation. _drawBottomBar now sizes the bar to the wrapped row count and draws row by row. panelGeometry() was extracted so pad/gap/radius follow whichever font the caption ended up in.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/share_card_renderer_test.dart group 'bottom-bar caption fits the card width'. The one that severs is 'no glyph is drawn in the right-hand padding of a 512px card': it RENDERS the real PNG for the exact spec stack_result_screen builds (M51 / Integration 00:35:00 / Frames 7 / Filter L at 512x512) over an opaque BLACK buffer so glyphs are the only bright pixels, then pixel-scans the right-hand padding across every text row and requires peak luminance < 120. The second test asserts fitCaption drops and reorders nothing (rows flattened == segments) and that every row measures within the bar.
revert_check: Severed the wiring at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/share_card_renderer.dart:475-477, replacing the fitCaption call with the pre-fix `final barFont = font; final rows = <List<String>>[segments];` (one row, height-derived font). The pixel-scan test failed. Restored -> 27/27 pass.
caveats: Cards narrower than a single segment at arial14 still clip that one segment - unrenderable at any size - but the rest of the caption is preserved rather than lost with it.

title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query - only an app restart clears it
summary: Two causes, both fixed. (1) Retry WAS already calling ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider) (first_light_view.dart:406-410, as the verifier corrected), but the provider returned a raw drift watch stream. Drift caches a query stream by its SQL, and a cached stream that has thrown stays thrown for the process lifetime - re-subscribing (all invalidate can do) replays the cached failure without re-executing the query. Confirmed in-process: fixing the row through the SAME database and invalidating still read back the original state. firstLightCandidatesProvider now yields a fresh one-shot dao.recentDetections() read first and then forwards the watch stream with .skip(1) (the drift replay is dropped because it can be STALER than the fresh read - raw statements and out-of-process writers never notify drift's stream store). (2) One undecodable row killed the whole feed: SQLite type affinity permits TEXT in an INTEGER column, so tile_id='tile-042' made the generated mapper throw FormatException and take the list with it. TransientDetectionsDao.watchRecentDetections/recentDetections now select raw QueryRows and map them through _mapSkippingUndecodable, which drops the bad row and keeps the rest.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/first_light_candidates_resilience_test.dart - a real NativeDatabase.memory with the bad row inserted via customStatement (the only way to get TEXT into an INTEGER column, exactly as an external tool would). 'a fixed row is picked up by a re-subscription, not only by a restart' does the whole reported sequence: subscribe -> fail, UPDATE the row through the same database, container.invalidate (what Retry does), re-subscribe, and requires the corrected row. The other three pin the one-bad-row tolerance for the watch stream, for a bad row that is NEWEST, and for the future read.
revert_check: Severed the wiring at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:148, replacing `_localFirstLightStream(...)` with the pre-fix `dao.watchRecentDetections(limit: kFirstLightFeedLimit)`. 'a fixed row is picked up by a re-subscription' failed with 'Bad state: No element' - the cached stream replayed the STALE tile-042 rows and the corrected row never arrived, exactly the reported 'only a restart clears it'. Restored -> 4/4 pass.
caveats: The verifier's second sub-claim ('the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched') was explicitly NOT confirmed and is not treated as a defect here - the underlying drift watch does push in-app writes; what it cannot see is an out-of-process edit, which is what the repro used. _mapSkippingUndecodable reports a skipped row with print() (the DAO layer has no logger; same pattern as migration_strategy.dart:62), so a persistently corrupt row prints once per stream emission on the debug console. Not user-facing. The .skip(1) leaves a narrow window: a detection written between the one-shot read completing and the watch subscription is dropped from the FIRST emission and only appears on the next table-update notification. First Light detections arrive per solved frame (minutes apart) and any later write re-emits, so this is negligible against the alternative, which is replaying a possibly-stale cached value and undoing the fresh read - the bug itself.

title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead, and only the selected network's blocker is explained
summary: Two causes. (1) A blocked chip was expressed as `onTap: null`, and SkotiqChip rendered that pixel-identically to an unselected-but-available chip - same fill, border and text colour, no Semantics, no cursor change - so three dead options read as three live ones. Added `enabled` to SkotiqChip (distinct from onTap==null, which means 'this was never an option, it is a status label'): dims fill/border/label, announces button + enabled:false + selected state, and shows the forbidden cursor. The panel now passes enabled: enabled. (2) The panel rendered _disabledReason ONLY for the currently-selected _format, and because a disabled chip has no onTap the user could never move the selection onto AAVSO or MPC - so both of those reasons were written and unreachable by any sequence of clicks. Replaced with _disabledNotices(), one labelled line per unavailable network ('AAVSO: ...', 'MPC: ...'), collapsing to a single line when the blocker is the DETECTION itself (not confirmed / dipole artefact) and therefore shared by all three.
test: Two suites. packages/skotiq_ui/test/skotiq_chip_disabled_test.dart (5 tests) covers the component: disabled colours differ and are dimmer, the semantics node carries isButton + hasEnabledState/isEnabled:false + selected state, a disabled chip swallows a tap, a plain status chip does NOT acquire a button role, and - added by me, because the shipped file did not cover the production combination - 'a disabled chip with no onTap is still a disabled option', which is exactly what the panel passes. packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_reasons_test.dart pumps the real panel on a fresh profile (no observer code, no MPC code, no TNS creds) and requires all three reasons on screen with NO interaction, plus - added by me - that every chip reports enabled == false. Second test pins the collapse-to-one-line case.
test_command: cd packages/skotiq_ui && flutter test; cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_reasons_test.dart
revert_check: Two severs. (a) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_panel.dart: deleted `enabled: enabled,` from the chip and put the notices block back to the single-reason form `_formatEnabled(_format,...) ? [] : [_disabledReason(_format,...)]` -> 'a disabled AAVSO and MPC chip each state their own reason' failed. (b) packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/components/skotiq_chip.dart:84: `if (onTap == null && enabled)` -> `if (onTap == null)`, i.e. the pre-fix early-out that swallows the disabled treatment for a chip with no onTap -> 'a disabled chip with no onTap is still a disabled option' failed. Both restored; skotiq_ui full suite 263/263 pass (shared design-system file), panel test 2/2.
caveats: Preview / Copy / Submit still just render as disabled SkotiqButtons (onPressed: null) rather than carrying their own reason; the per-network notice block above them now names the blocker, which is the information that was missing.

title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude ('mag 2.4  NAKED EYE')
summary: transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 was `final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();`, passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude - the APPARENT magnitude field every alert surface consumes (transient_card buckets it NAKED EYE <=6 / BINOCULAR <=10 / SMALL SCOPE <=14, the feed filters on magnitudeThreshold, shouldNotify auto-queues at or under autoQueueMagnitude, addAlertToTargets copies it into the target library). A difference-image pipeline measures only delta_mag against the atlas template and there is no photometric zero point behind it - the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all - and since a difference larger than ~6 mag is essentially impossible, EVERY self-discovery with a measured delta was announced naked-eye or binocular. magnitude is now null; the change itself is carried in the classification line as 'delta2.35 mag brighter than template' (or 'fainter'), and the notes state in words that it is a brightness change and not an apparent magnitude. Verified every consumer already guards on null: transient_card.dart:164 gates the whole chip on `magnitude != null`, and TransientAlertService.shouldNotify wraps both the threshold and the auto-queue test in `if (alert.magnitude != null)`.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper_test.dart - 'never reports a delta magnitude as an apparent magnitude' (magnitude and peakMagnitude both null for delta_mag -2.35), 'a delta this large would be announced as naked-eye if kept' (states the consequence explicitly), 'surfaces the brightness change in the classification line' (delta2.35 mag brighter present, 'mag 2.4' absent; and the fainter direction), 'a detection with no measured delta keeps a plain classification', 'the notes say plainly that the delta is not a magnitude', and the catalog-matched case.
revert_check: Restored the pre-fix assignment at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:48, `magnitude: null` -> `magnitude: detection.deltaMag?.abs()`. 3 tests failed. Restored -> 54/54 in test/services/transients/ pass.
caveats: No apparent magnitude is computed - there is no zero point to compute one from. The alert simply stops claiming one. If photometric_transforms ever carries a solved zero point for the detection's frame, that is the place to populate magnitude for real.

title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it ('Confirmed' on one sub-tab, 'New' on the next)
summary: The verifier's correction was right and load-bearing: the alert list IS rebuilt (activeTransientAlertsProvider listens to the drift watchRecentDetections live query, which re-emits on the local markReviewed write) and transient_alert_mapper DOES map reviewed -> acknowledged. The badge stayed 'New' because the Observing Alerts UI never read the alert's own state: transients_screen watched transientAlertStatesProvider and did `states[alert.id]`, and TransientCard falls back to newAlert when that map has no entry. That map is populated ONLY from `transient_alert_state_<id>` settings rows written by the user's own queue/observe/dismiss actions - nothing ever seeds it from TransientAlert.state - so the mapper's `acknowledged` was dead on this surface. Added resolveTransientAlertState(alert, overrides) => overrides[alert.id] ?? alert.state, and routed the card, all three filter branches and unacknowledgedAlertCountProvider through it. A user action still wins (that is what an override is) and API-sourced alerts carry the default newAlert, so their behaviour is unchanged.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transients_confirmed_state_test.dart - builds the alert through the real transientAlertFromDetection from a reviewed=true detection (so the mapping under test is the production one), pumps the real TransientsView, and asserts the card is not badged 'New'; a second test pins that an unreviewed detection still IS New (so the fix is not a blanket suppression); a third switches to the 'New' filter and requires the confirmed detection to be absent from it.
revert_check: Severed both wiring sites in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart: :180 `resolveTransientAlertState(alert, states)` -> `states[alert.id]`, and the newAlerts filter branch back to `state == null || state == TransientAlertState.newAlert`. 'a confirmed detection is not badged New on Observing Alerts' and 'a confirmed detection does not sit under the New filter' both failed. Restored -> 8/8 in test/screens/transients/ pass.
caveats: The finding's own `where` (transient_alert_provider.dart, 'the alert list is not invalidated') was wrong; the cause and the fix are in transients_screen.dart plus the new resolver in transient_alert_provider.dart.
